headline: Bilawal urges PM to mend ties with allies, avoid opposition clash
description: PPP will support government in tackling economic crisis as Sindh completes one million homes for flood victims, says party chairman
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari has urged Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to restore the confidence of coalition partners instead of opening a new front against the opposition, saying his party will support the government in addressing the economic crisis.

“Until all Pakistanis stand united, we will not be able to protect the people from this difficult situation,” Bilawal said while addressing a ceremony in Karachi on Tuesday to mark the completion of one million homes for flood victims under the Sindh Peoples Housing Scheme.

Bilawal described the initiative as one of the largest housing projects in the world, saying the Sindh government had completed the construction of one million homes, with the total expected to reach two million by the time the project is completed.

The PPP chairman said the project had been carried out with support from the federal government and international partners.

He added that one million families had been granted land ownership under the initiative, describing it as the largest land transfer programme since 1970.

Bilawal said the PPP had also provided ownership rights to farmers, adding that home ownership would offer economic security to poor families.

He said the housing initiative fulfilled the party’s promise of providing “roti, kapra aur makan” (food, clothing and shelter).

Political parties must help people overcome economic crisis

Bilawal said people across the world were facing an economic crisis, with citizens looking towards governments for relief.

He said every initiative undertaken by the Sindh government was aimed at serving the public and reducing the economic burden on people.

“People are not looking at how governments will make them fight among themselves. They are looking at how governments will support them during the economic crisis,” he said.

The PPP chairman said political parties were responsible for helping people overcome economic hardships rather than spreading hatred.

He criticised politicians who believed that making the business community wealthier would lead to national development, saying governments and political parties must prioritise the welfare of ordinary citizens.

Bilawal thanked PM Shehbaz for supporting the housing project, saying the federal government had extended assistance to the Sindh government.

He contrasted the support with the response of the previous government, saying no financial assistance had been provided when floods struck Pakistan during its tenure.

Bilawal said Pakistan would have to reset its political landscape to overcome the challenges facing the country.

“I urge Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to restore the confidence of his coalition partners and establish an atmosphere of trust instead of starting new confrontations with the opposition,” he said.

He reiterated that the PPP would support the government in tackling the economic crisis.

Bilawal challenges opponents to find corruption in housing project

Bilawal challenged political opponents to identify corruption in the housing scheme, saying he was confident that no corruption had taken place in the project.

He urged Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah to request an audit of the initiative by international organisations monitoring corruption.

The PPP chairman said the Sindh government was frequently accused of corruption, while critics also pointed to the province’s education crisis.

“People should at least ask us why these problems exist,” he said.

Bilawal urged other provinces to learn from Sindh’s initiatives for public welfare, saying the provincial government’s projects were designed to help people overcome economic difficulties.

headline: Sri Lanka struggle to 114-3 after Pakistan's first Test declaration
description: Debutant Saqib Khan takes 2-54, and Mohammad Abbas strikes early as the visitors trail by 320 runs in Rawalpindi
author: AFP
article_text:
Debutant pace bowler Saqib Khan grabbed two wickets as Sri Lanka struggled to 114-3 by the end of day two of the opening Test after Pakistan declared at 434-9 in Rawalpindi on Tuesday.

Saqib dismissed Dinesh Chandimal for one in his second over and then removed a well-set Lahiru Udara for 42 to leave Sri Lanka on 65-3.

His experienced pace partner Mohammad Abbas took the first wicket, having opener Pasindu Sooriyabandara caught behind for a duck in the third over.

Kamindu Mendis (40) and Dhananjaya de Silva (22) were unbeaten at the close, with Sri Lanka still trailing by 320 runs on the first innings.

Bad light again stopped play 25 minutes before schedule.

De Silva was dropped by spinner Arafat Minhas in the penultimate over of the day.

Saqib had the figures of 2-54, while Abbas took 1-23.

Pakistan middle-order batter Saud Shakeel earlier missed his century by seven runs, a miscued hook off Asitha Fernando giving wicketkeeper Kusal Mendis his fifth catch in the innings.

Shakeel, who became Fernando’s 100th wicket in 29 Tests, hit nine boundaries in his 199-ball innings.

He lifted Pakistan from 281-5 overnight with a resolute 96-run stand with Ghazi Ghori for the sixth wicket. Ghori scored a confident 48.

Shakeel said he was disappointed at missing a fifth Test century.

“Yes, you get disappointed when you miss a milestone, and it looks bad,” said Shakeel. “But we have put up a good total with Arafat chipping in with a half-century.”

Sri Lankan fielding coach Jordan Gregory hoped his batters would show grit to match Pakistan’s total.

“We have to take the match session by session and hope that the Kamindu-De Silva partnership goes on and make a match of it because the pitch has enough to produce a result,” said Gregory.

Debutant Minhas made a stylish 52, the fifth half-century of the innings, that included nine boundaries and a six.

Sri Lanka had hoped for early wickets but struggled on a seemingly hard and green pitch, despite taking the second new ball after 80 overs.

Dilshan Madushanka finally made the breakthrough when Ghori edged him to gully, where Sooriyabandara held a low catch.

Pace bowlers Fernando and Madushanka were the pick of the Sri Lanka attack, both taking three wickets.

The second and final Test is in Lahore from November 17.

Kamindu Mendis (40) and Dhananjaya de Silva (22) were unbeaten at the close, with Sri Lanka still trailing by 320 runs on the first innings.
Bad light again stopped play 25 minutes before schedule.
De Silva was dropped by spinner Arafat Minhas in the penultimate over of the day.
Saqib had the figures of 2-54, while Abbas took 1-23.
Pakistan middle-order batter Saud Shakeel earlier missed his century by seven runs, a miscued hook off Asitha Fernando giving wicketkeeper Kusal Mendis his fifth catch in the innings.
Shakeel, who became Fernando’s 100th wicket in 29 Tests, hit nine boundaries in his 199-ball innings.
He lifted Pakistan from 281-5 overnight with a resolute 96-run stand with Ghazi Ghori for the sixth wicket. Ghori scored a confident 48.
Shakeel said he was disappointed at missing a fifth Test century.
“Yes, you get disappointed when you miss a milestone, and it looks bad,” said Shakeel. “But we have put up a good total with Arafat chipping in with a half-century.”
Sri Lankan fielding coach Jordan Gregory hoped his batters would show grit to match Pakistan’s total.
“We have to take the match session by session and hope that the Kamindu-De Silva partnership goes on and make a match of it because the pitch has enough to produce a result,” said Gregory.
Debutant Minhas made a stylish 52, the fifth half-century of the innings, that included nine boundaries and a six.
Sri Lanka had hoped for early wickets but struggled on a seemingly hard and green pitch, despite taking the second new ball after 80 overs.
Dilshan Madushanka finally made the breakthrough when Ghori edged him to gully, where Sooriyabandara held a low catch.
Pace bowlers Fernando and Madushanka were the pick of the Sri Lanka attack, both taking three wickets.
The second and final Test is in Lahore from November 17.

headline: New Israeli parliament to take aim at Netanyahu as Eisenkot seeks government
description: Eisenkot, handed the initial mandate to form a government, vows a ‘national-emergency government’ as quickly as possible
author: AFP
article_text:
Israel’s new parliament is prepared to be sworn in Tuesday with a mission to take aim immediately at caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, as rival Gadi Eisenkot vowed quickly to cobble together a new government.

President Isaac Herzog will deliver a speech at 4:00 pm (1400 GMT) for the swearing-in of the 120-seat parliament, in which neither Netanyahu’s right-wing coalition nor Eisenkot’s broad left-to-right anti-Netanyahu bloc will hold a majority.

“I am committed in this complex situation to form a national-emergency government as quickly as possible,” Eisenkot, a 66-year-old former military chief who only recently entered politics, said as he prepared to be sworn in.

Eisenkot’s allies hope to use their newfound legislative power to move rapidly on key priorities, including a commission to investigate security failures under Netanyahu that allowed the October 7, 2023 attack by Hamas, the deadliest day in Israel’s history.

Herzog on Sunday gave Eisenkot the initial mandate to form a government, starting the clock for him to cobble together a coalition within 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension.

Ahead of the opening of the parliament, known as the Knesset, Eisenkot’s party announced agreements on key people to replace allies of Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, who has been in and out of office for nearly 20 years.

Eisenkot’s bloc announced it would put forward as parliament speaker Matan Kahana, a former senior military figure who clashed with ultra-Orthodox Jews in a past stint in government.

Avigdor Liberman, a right-wing member of Eisenkot’s bloc who has played a key role in deciding who can enter the government, will be nominated as chair of the foreign affairs and defence committee.

Arab-Israeli lawmakers said they would support Kahana, all but guaranteeing he will take the most votes and, with it, the helm of the parliament.

Parties representing the Arab minority — descendants of Palestinians who stayed after Israel’s creation in 1948 — won a record number of seats in the October 27 election on the back of anger over Netanyahu’s hard-right government.

But Eisenkot needs 61 votes — a majority — to become prime minister. Liberman has made clear that he will refuse to join a government that relies on Arab-Israelis, even if they stay out of the coalition and prop up a government without a majority.

“A minority government would only lead to the return of Netanyahu with 70 members of the Knesset,” Liberman told reporters.

Arab-Israeli lawmakers under fire

Netanyahu has accused Arab-Israeli parties of supporting Hamas and accepting foreign funding, allegations the lawmakers deny and call smear tactics.

Liberman, a former aide to Netanyahu turned critic who shares hawkish views, said he would use his new position to investigate allegations of foreign funding to the parties.

Entering parliament, Mansour Abbas, leader of the Israeli-Arab party Raam, rejected Netanyahu’s accusations of fraud by Israeli-Arab parties and pointed out that Netanyahu faces corruption charges which could land him in jail if he loses power.

“We will keep up the process of replacing the government,” Abbas told reporters. “We aspire to be part of the solution.”

Abbas confirmed he supports a two-state solution with the Palestinians, a stance shared by neither Netanyahu nor Eisenkot, a former military chief who has sought to appeal to the centre.

Shunning Israeli Arabs, Liberman has instead proposed an alliance with ultra-Orthodox Jews, despite his years of bitter denunciations of the community for its singular priority on maintaining an exemption from mandatory military service.

Eisenkot’s core bloc has 48 seats, but would achieve a majority if the 19 Arab-Israeli lawmakers either enter the government or, more likely, vote for it without joining.

The two ultra-Orthodox parties hold 13 seats. United Torah Judaism, which has seven seats, has stopped short of recommitting to Netanyahu, leaving Israel’s longest-serving prime minister with 46 seats.

The two parties were long allied with Netanyahu, who backed the exemption from military service without enshrining it fully into law.

An alliance with either group would likely be fragile, with a small number of lawmakers able to bring Eisenkot down over their particular concerns.

headline: Remittances hit $3.9bn in October, up 14% on year
description: Inflows from Saudi Arabia, the UAE and the UK drive growth as SBP raises its full-year forecast to $45bn
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Overseas Pakistanis sent home $3.89 billion in October 2026, up 13.8% from $3.42 billion a year earlier, the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) said on Tuesday.

Remittances were also 8.5% higher than September’s $3.6 billion.

Cumulative inflows for July-October of FY27 rose 14% to $14.8 billion, from $13 billion in the same period last year.

“These sustained inflows are strengthening Pakistan’s foreign exchange position, supporting households and reinforcing external-account stability,” Khurram Schehzad, advisor to the finance minister, said on X.

Remittances support the external account and boost the incomes of households that depend on them.

Last month, the SBP raised its projections for remittances and foreign exchange reserves, citing stronger inflows and a better external-account outlook.

Speaking at a press conference on the monetary policy decision, SBP Governor Jameel Ahmed said remittances had remained resilient in the first quarter of FY27 and would come in higher than earlier estimates.

“Workers’ remittances are expected to increase further, with Pakistan’s inflows projected at $45 billion in the current fiscal year, up from the previous estimate of $44 billion,” he added.

Major corridors

Saudi Arabia was the largest source, with $982 million in October. That was up 17% from $838 million a year earlier and 9% from $899 million in September.

Inflows from the United Arab Emirates rose 16% year-on-year, from $703 million to $816 million. They were up 9% from $749 million in September.

Remittances from the UK totalled $592 million, up 19% from $499 million a year earlier.

The US sent $329 million, up 9% from $301 million a year earlier and 8% from $306 million in September.

Remittances from European Union countries reached $461 million, up 3% from $448 million in September.

Overseas Pakistanis sent home $3.89 billion in October 2026, up 13.8% from $3.42 billion a year earlier, the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) said on Tuesday.

Remittances were also 8.5% higher than September’s $3.6 billion.

Cumulative inflows for July-October of FY27 rose 14% to $14.8 billion, from $13 billion in the same period last year.

“These sustained inflows are strengthening Pakistan’s foreign exchange position, supporting households and reinforcing external-account stability,” Khurram Schehzad, advisor to the finance minister, said on X.

Remittances support the external account and boost the incomes of households that depend on them.

Last month, the SBP raised its projections for remittances and foreign exchange reserves, citing stronger inflows and a better external-account outlook.

Speaking at a press conference on the monetary policy decision, SBP Governor Jameel Ahmed said remittances had remained resilient in the first quarter of FY27 and would come in higher than earlier estimates.

“Workers’ remittances are expected to increase further, with Pakistan’s inflows projected at $45 billion in the current fiscal year, up from the previous estimate of $44 billion,” he added.

Major corridors

Saudi Arabia was the largest source, with $982 million in October. That was up 17% from $838 million a year earlier and 9% from $899 million in September.

Inflows from the United Arab Emirates rose 16% year-on-year, from $703 million to $816 million. They were up 9% from $749 million in September.

Remittances from the UK totalled $592 million, up 19% from $499 million a year earlier.

The US sent $329 million, up 9% from $301 million a year earlier and 8% from $306 million in September.

Remittances from European Union countries reached $461 million, up 3% from $448 million in September.

headline: Rubio tells G7 US will keep imposing 'devastating' costs on Iran, diplomats say
description: Rubio briefs G7 foreign ministers on Iran conflict; he refers to Iranian authorities as 'lunatics', two G7 diplomats say
author: Reuters
article_text:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio ‌told G7 foreign ministers on Tuesday that the US would keep imposing “devastating” economic costs on Iran, saying it had options beyond war or agreeing to unacceptable Iranian demands, four G7 diplomats said.

Rubio’s comments came during a meeting in Paris of foreign ministers from the Group of ​Seven, which comprises Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States, as well ​as the European Union.

The diplomats said Rubio had used strong language to describe the ⁠Iranian authorities. Two said he had referred to them as “lunatics”.

The diplomats quoted Rubio as saying that, rather ​than resuming the war or accepting Iran’s demands, Washington’s current policy of tough economic sanctions is working ​and is limiting Tehran’s ability to fund its regional activities and proxies.

“Rubio said that they will continue with… (imposing) devastating economic operating costs on Iran,” said one of the diplomats, who all spoke on condition of anonymity.

Rubio’s comments came a day after ​US President Donald Trump said he planned to hold off on new military strikes against Iran for the ​time being after appeals from countries in the region, including from Qatar’s prime minister in White House talks.

Trump also ‌said he ⁠plans to keep up a naval blockade on Iran in the Strait of Hormuz for now.

QATAR’S PM IS IN PARIS AFTER MEETING TRUMP

After his talks with Trump, Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al-Thani, a key intermediary with Iran, made an unscheduled stop at the meeting of G7 foreign ministers in Paris. He met ​there with the ministers ​of the European countries ⁠and Saudi Arabia.

According to two European diplomats, Sheikh Mohammed expressed cautious optimism after his talks in Washington that a diplomatic solution to the crisis was still ​possible rather than a further escalation of the conflict.

Some of Trump’s top advisers, ​including Rubio, ⁠newly installed White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, back the policy of maintaining heavy economic pressure on Iran, according to one of the diplomats.

Vice President JD Vance, who ⁠has ​blamed Republican losses in last week’s midterm elections on the Iran ​war, prefers a deal with Iran, but Trump for now believes that a tenable deal is not possible, the person said.

The ​White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

headline: Maryam warns ministers against corruption, vows no leniency
description: Punjab CM says she will not spare any minister facing a substantiated corruption complaint, as she distributes laptops and scholarships among students in Jhelum
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz has warned members of her cabinet against corruption, saying she will not spare any minister if a complaint backed by evidence is brought against them.

“I swear that if anyone comes to me with a corruption complaint against any of my ministers, I will not spare them,” she said while addressing a ceremony in Jhelum on Tuesday to distribute laptops and Honhaar scholarships among students.

CM Maryam said no one would be allowed to misuse public money, adding that she remained accountable to the people of Punjab.

She said she had never claimed that corruption had been eliminated from the province, but maintained that Punjab was the only province where the chief minister personally detected corruption cases and pursued them.

“Every day, I come across some form of corruption and follow it up,” she said.

The chief minister also questioned whether corruption was not taking place in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Sindh and Balochistan, asking why such cases were not being pursued with the same vigour.

Maryam aims at political opponents

CM Maryam said Punjab was progressing and development work was underway across the province.

She said some people had started feeling uncomfortable as elections approached, adding that those who had not delivered any development projects found it easier to level corruption allegations against others.

“Those who have not done even a single penny’s worth of work find it easy to accuse others of corruption,” she said.

Referring to recent by-elections, she said banned organisations had made every effort to secure victories, but the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) had emerged successful.

She said public service could not be challenged by any political narrative.

CM Maryam also questioned why those criticising the government continued to serve as ministers instead of resigning, saying some politicians were trying to secure their positions for their turn in power.

She added that the arrogance of power and money would no longer prevail in Punjab.

The chief minister said her government had launched development projects worth trillions of rupees over the past three years and challenged critics to identify even one project involving corruption.

She also accused the previous governments in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa of allowing corruption to flourish for years.

Maryam said popularity did not require a political narrative, adding that people knew development took place under PML-N governments.

Scholarships, laptops and scooters for students

Addressing students at the ceremony, Maryam said she had come to reward them for their hard work.

She said the students deserved the scholarships and laptops, while their parents also deserved recognition for their sacrifices.

The chief minister said 109 students in Jhelum had received Honhaar scholarships.

She added that the provincial government was preparing to distribute 100,000 scooters among students in December, with recipients also receiving formal training.

CM Maryam said Punjab was the only province providing extensive support to young people.

She claimed that government schools in Punjab were performing better than private schools and said green buses operating in Lahore were being introduced in other cities.

The chief minister said the government had ended the practice of concentrating development projects in major cities, adding that people from other areas were now travelling to Jhelum for cardiac treatment.

She also referred to an incident in which a shopkeeper allegedly assaulted a girl, saying the victim had been called to a police station and asked to slap the wealthy shopkeeper.

CM Maryam said her government was standing with the poor and the vulnerable, adding that students had also been provided free travel on green buses.

headline: Memes and jokes flood social media over Nvidia CEO’s alleged Chinese spy scandal
description: Users react with humour and speculation after Jensen Huang acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife, and Nvidia opened an investigation
author: Umair Ali
article_text:
Social media users are turning the scandal around Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang into memes, jokes and commentary, after reports that he had a relationship with an alleged Chinese spy, an allegation China has denied.

Much of the early commentary centred on an X post by user Aaron Bennett, captioned “I’m seeing a pattern here,” which placed photos of Huang and other technology executives beside images of their asian partners.

One reply came from X user Zack, also known as Twitch streamer Asmongold, who started streaming in 2011 and is one of the platform’s top streamers. He is also a YouTuber and has an asian girlfriend. His reply to Bennett’s post read “They can’t all be spies…right???”.

Similar posts, including one on Instagram titled “Silicon Valley billionaires have a type,” circulated on other platforms. No news reports allege that the other executives or their partners have intelligence links.

Memes mocking Huang are flooding X, led by an AI-generated Coldplay kiss-cam clip, and some posts joke that the AI videos were made on Nvidia chips. Some creators have labelled their posts as satire.

Some users joked about being Chinese spies themselves, with posts inviting any billionaire seeking an affair to send a direct message. Some Asian women also posted videos and messages saying, in jest, that they were not Chinese spies.

Other posts lean on spy-movie humour. An Instagram clip with a reaction image joked about a new acquaintance suddenly asking about a company’s trade secrets.

Fans of the Harry Potter series also joined in with posts shows Harry and a his asian love interest with a caption joking that the Ministry of Magic had once sent a Chinese spy to get him arrested.

Another post showed a person laughing as they watched from the sidelines, with a caption: “OpenAI CEO Sam Altman ….., looking on as other technology executives are honey trapped by Chinese spy girls.

Huang said in a memo to Nvidia employees on November 8 that he had been unfaithful to his wife, NBC News reported. “I was unfaithful to my wife,” he said.

Other posts speculated that Huang could face an $81 billion divorce settlement without a prenuptial agreement, or recirculated a claim that his wife pawned her wedding ring in 1995 to keep Nvidia afloat. Neither claim has been verified.

Reuters reported that Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, held senior roles at a Shanghai investment firm before becoming the controlling shareholder of Singapore-based cloud-computing company Megaspeed International, which lists itself as an Nvidia business partner. She is not related to Jensen Huang.

The New York Times reported in October that US authorities had concluded she was a Chinese intelligence asset who passed information to Beijing while building a close relationship with the Nvidia CEO. Reuters could not independently verify the intelligence allegation, which China has denied.

Nvidia’s board has opened an independent investigation into reports that its CEO was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation, but said it had no reason to believe national security information or company trade secrets were compromised. Without commenting directly on Alice Huang, Jensen Huang acknowledged on Sunday being unfaithful to his wife, but said he was committed to supporting US national security.

President Donald Trump said on Monday that the FBI was also looking into the matter, and that Huang told him he had no idea the woman was a spy. Megaspeed has drawn scrutiny from US authorities over suspicions it helped Chinese companies obtain restricted Nvidia chips, but there has been no public finding that it violated the rules, according to Reuters.

headline: Embattled Pentagon chief slams impeachment effort as 'farce'
description: Trump gives Hegseth an ‘A’ PLUS, PLUS, PLUS as Republican Rep. Thomas Massie’s articles accuse him of war powers violations
author: AFP
article_text:
US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth on Tuesday denounced a push to impeach him as a “farce” and defended his record leading multiple military operations that have sparked allegations of misconduct against the Pentagon chief.

Under pressure after President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance blamed the Iran war for the Republican Party’s sweeping losses in midterm elections, Hegseth now faces a congressional effort to remove him from office.

“It’s a farce, and it’s a stunt, and everybody knows it,” a defiant Hegseth told journalists of the impeachment proceedings launched by Representative Thomas Massie, a Republican, the previous day.

“What one disgruntled and defeated congressman is attempting is not oversight, and it’s not accountability. It’s a political spectacle,” Hegseth said.

Massie, a fierce critic of Trump, is leaving office after losing a primary contest to a candidate backed by the president.

Trump has backed Hegseth so far, and on Tuesday wrote on social media that the Pentagon chief “gets an ‘A’ PLUS, PLUS, PLUS for his defence” against the impeachment efforts.

Hegseth on Tuesday defended military interventions in Yemen, Iran and Venezuela as well as strikes targeting alleged drug-smuggling boats in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific.

‘Would do it again’

“I stand behind every one of these operations. I was proud to execute them, and I would do it again tomorrow,” he said, equating the effort to remove him with an attack on US troops.

“These resolutions tell everyone of them that their service was a crime. Their service was not a crime. These are heroes,” said Hegseth.

Several of the articles of impeachment relate to the Iran war, accusing Hegseth of violating the War Powers Resolution, which requires congressional consultation on US military interventions.

Hegseth is a staunch defender of the widely unpopular war against Iran, which he has described as a “courageous and historic effort.”

The 2025 conflict with Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis also features in Massie’s articles of impeachment, which charge Hegseth with starting the operation without congressional approval and in the absence of an imminent threat to the United States.

Massie also branded strikes on alleged drug-smuggling boats in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific as “extrajudicial killings” and said Hegseth “chilled independent legal review within the Department of Defence.”

And he accused Hegseth of suppressing free speech by trying to punish Democratic Senator Mark Kelly over a video in which he and other lawmakers urged military and intelligence personnel to refuse illegal orders.

“Using the powers of his office, Secretary Hegseth retaliated against and sought to intimidate United States Senator Mark Kelly for his statement,” one of the articles of impeachment said.

article_html:
US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth on Tuesday denounced a push to impeach him as a “farce” and defended his record leading multiple military operations that have sparked allegations of misconduct against the Pentagon chief.

Under pressure after President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance blamed the Iran war for the Republican Party’s sweeping losses in midterm elections, Hegseth now faces a congressional effort to remove him from office.

“It’s a farce, and it’s a stunt, and everybody knows it,” a defiant Hegseth told journalists of the impeachment proceedings launched by Representative Thomas Massie, a Republican, the previous day.

“What one disgruntled and defeated congressman is attempting is not oversight, and it’s not accountability. It’s a political spectacle,” Hegseth said.

Massie, a fierce critic of Trump, is leaving office after losing a primary contest to a candidate backed by the president.

Trump has backed Hegseth so far, and on Tuesday wrote on social media that the Pentagon chief “gets an ‘A’ PLUS, PLUS, PLUS for his defence” against the impeachment efforts.

Hegseth on Tuesday defended military interventions in Yemen, Iran and Venezuela as well as strikes targeting alleged drug-smuggling boats in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific.

‘Would do it again’

“I stand behind every one of these operations. I was proud to execute them, and I would do it again tomorrow,” he said, equating the effort to remove him with an attack on US troops.

“These resolutions tell everyone of them that their service was a crime. Their service was not a crime. These are heroes,” said Hegseth.

Several of the articles of impeachment relate to the Iran war, accusing Hegseth of violating the War Powers Resolution, which requires congressional consultation on US military interventions.

Hegseth is a staunch defender of the widely unpopular war against Iran, which he has described as a “courageous and historic effort.”

The 2025 conflict with Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis also features in Massie’s articles of impeachment, which charge Hegseth with starting the operation without congressional approval and in the absence of an imminent threat to the United States.

Massie also branded strikes on alleged drug-smuggling boats in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific as “extrajudicial killings” and said Hegseth “chilled independent legal review within the Department of Defence.”

And he accused Hegseth of suppressing free speech by trying to punish Democratic Senator Mark Kelly over a video in which he and other lawmakers urged military and intelligence personnel to refuse illegal orders.

“Using the powers of his office, Secretary Hegseth retaliated against and sought to intimidate United States Senator Mark Kelly for his statement,” one of the articles of impeachment said.

headline: Anthropic eyes $1.4 trillion IPO valuation in test of Wall Street's AI fervor
description: Cornerstone investors include Google, Nvidia and AMD
author: Reuters
article_text:
Anthropic’s blockbuster IPO is set to give the company a valuation of up to $1.4 trillion, slightly lower than some investors’ expectations amid a recent cooling in investor appetite for AI, setting up a defining test of Wall Street’s faith in the boom that it helped ignite.

The AI lab best ​known for its Claude chatbot, and some of its investors, are aiming to raise up to $64.4 billion by selling 825 million shares in the IPO priced up to $78 per share.

Anthropic will also raise $26 billion via a separate private placement deal with ‌cornerstone investors such as Alphabet’s Google, Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices.

The company is launching the roadshow for a historic share sale that is expected to set a benchmark for the sector, following years of hype that fueled a massive influx of capital into AI companies.

“What we are seeing is essentially a reassessment of Anthropic’s value in a more challenging AI environment,” said Ipek Ozkardeskaya, senior analyst at Swissquote Bank in Geneva. “The company continues to post impressive growth, but investors are increasingly focused on the cost of generating that growth.”

At the top of the price range, Anthropic would be valued at about $1.4 trillion on a fully diluted basis, which includes securities such as stock options and restricted stock. On ​a non-diluted basis, excluding those securities, the company’s market value would be about $1 trillion.

Hours before Anthropic filed an updated prospectus with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on Tuesday, details of its IPO, including the proposed price range, were briefly circulated to investment ​banks late on Monday shortly before being retracted, according to emails seen by Reuters.

The preliminary terms showed Anthropic planned to sell about 867 million shares at up to $80 apiece, in an offering that could raise as much ⁠as $69.3 billion, including shares sold by existing shareholders.

The prospectus ultimately filed with the SEC contained different terms, with Anthropic setting a lower price range and targeting reduced proceeds.

Big spend concerns

Nvidia joined the deal amid an FBI probe into its CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with a Chinese woman alleged ​to be a spy for Beijing, which has also triggered an internal investigation.

Investors had previously discussed a valuation of as much as $2 trillion, but expectations have since come down given the company’s substantial infrastructure commitments and the recent volatility in AI-related stocks, with the $1.5 trillion figure viewed as the high end ​of the range, Reuters previously reported.

“The shift from a $2 trillion valuation to today’s level reflects a change in focus from revenue growth alone to the significant financial commitments and spending required to sustain it,” Ozkardeskaya said.

Investors are also closely watching Anthropic’s IPO for clues about rival OpenAI, which is seeking to raise $30 billion in what is expected to be its final private funding round before a potential IPO early next year. OpenAI recently secured $11 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation, below the $1.5 trillion it had initially sought.

The second half of the year has brought a reckoning for the AI boom, as investors question whether returns will justify the massive spending and mounting debt costs in an elevated ​interest-rate environment.

Concerns are also rising over the sustainability of the investment cycle, with questions around circular financing arrangements, the risk of infrastructure overcapacity and how quickly companies can turn their AI investments into revenue.

The Nasdaq notched its Deepest one-day drop in 19 months on Thursday, wiping out trillions in market value on ​fears of more AI scrutiny, particularly on data centre construction, after Democrats’ massive gains in the US midterm elections.

‘Harmful actions’

Despite the midterms being widely viewed as a rebuff to a White House which has aggressively supported the AI build-out and opposed regulations, Anthropic adopted President Donald Trump’s preferred name for the new technology, “Super Intelligence”, ‌at several points in ⁠its IPO filing.

Its filing spoke of a vision to “bring forth an age of miracles,” even as it warned of existential risks to humanity, laying bare the extraordinary promise and profound uncertainties at the heart of the AI boom.

The prospectus outlined a range of risks facing both the company and the technology, warning that competitors could gain an edge by developing models faster and that advances in AI could outpace Anthropic’s ability to put adequate safety and security measures in place.

“Our models have in the past behaved, and may in the future behave, in unintended, misaligned, or autonomous ways, including by taking harmful actions that no user or third party directed, which could adversely affect our reputation and brand, business, financial condition, and results of operations,” Anthropic warned in its latest prospectus.

The warnings come amid a growing number of incidents involving “rogue” AI agents that have escaped sandboxed environments and breached private company systems, alongside concerns that ​increasingly capable AI tools could be used by hackers to penetrate protected ​networks.

Growth comes with risks

Greater oversight and potential regulatory hurdles could complicate ⁠the infrastructure buildout underpinning the AI boom.

But Anthropic’s growth has so far defied those concerns, propelled by surging demand for its products, particularly its viral Claude models.

Anthropic’s run-rate revenue was roughly $81 billion as of October 31, up $10 billion from September 30, according to the IPO filing.

Anthropic’s net loss narrowed in the third quarter as revenue jumped 47% from a quarter earlier to $16.96 billion, though the pace of growth slowed. It had surged 144% in the prior ​quarter.

The company attributed the breakneck growth to the rapid adoption of Claude, including specialised products targeting industries such as healthcare, financial services and legal services.

Anthropic’s ambitions also come with enormous infrastructure costs. The company has ​nearly $900 billion in computing commitments with partners including ⁠Amazon and Alphabet’s Google, highlighting how its rapid growth depends on securing vast amounts of future computing capacity, some of which relies on financing beyond the company’s control.

The listing move follows Elon Musk’s SpaceX raising $75 billion in the world’s largest IPO in June, at a valuation of nearly $1.75 trillion, excluding additional shares purchased by underwriters through the greenshoe option.

Together with investments from cornerstones, which include Broadcom, Micron Technology, Microsoft and TSMC, the Anthropic share offering will raise a total of up to $90.4 billion.

Certain Anthropic board members and entities affiliated or associated with them have indicated interest in buying up to $303 million of shares from the offering.

Anthropic, locked in ⁠a fierce battle ​for market share with rival OpenAI, was last valued at $965 billion in a private funding round. The company’s prominent investors include Altimeter Capital, Dragoneer, Greenoaks and Sequoia Capital.

Anthropic, led by CEO ​Dario Amodei, was founded in 2021 by a group of researchers who left OpenAI following disagreements over governance and AI safety.

The shares are expected to trade on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol “ANT” after the IPO closes, which would make Anthropic one of the few major companies to go public this fall as higher borrowing costs, geopolitical turmoil and rising bond ​yields weigh on the IPO market.

Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are leading the syndicate of investment banks underwriting the offering.

Anthropic will also raise $26 billion via a separate private placement deal with ‌cornerstone investors such as Alphabet’s Google, Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices.

The company is launching the roadshow for a historic share sale that is expected to set a benchmark for the sector, following years of hype that fueled a massive influx of capital into AI companies.

“What we are seeing is essentially a reassessment of Anthropic’s value in a more challenging AI environment,” said Ipek Ozkardeskaya, senior analyst at Swissquote Bank in Geneva. “The company continues to post impressive growth, but investors are increasingly focused on the cost of generating that growth.”

At the top of the price range, Anthropic would be valued at about $1.4 trillion on a fully diluted basis, which includes securities such as stock options and restricted stock. On ​a non-diluted basis, excluding those securities, the company’s market value would be about $1 trillion.

Hours before Anthropic filed an updated prospectus with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on Tuesday, details of its IPO, including the proposed price range, were briefly circulated to investment ​banks late on Monday shortly before being retracted, according to emails seen by Reuters.

The preliminary terms showed Anthropic planned to sell about 867 million shares at up to $80 apiece, in an offering that could raise as much ⁠as $69.3 billion, including shares sold by existing shareholders.

The prospectus ultimately filed with the SEC contained different terms, with Anthropic setting a lower price range and targeting reduced proceeds.

Big spend concerns

Nvidia joined the deal amid an FBI probe into its CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with a Chinese woman alleged ​to be a spy for Beijing, which has also triggered an internal investigation.

Investors had previously discussed a valuation of as much as $2 trillion, but expectations have since come down given the company’s substantial infrastructure commitments and the recent volatility in AI-related stocks, with the $1.5 trillion figure viewed as the high end ​of the range, Reuters previously reported.

“The shift from a $2 trillion valuation to today’s level reflects a change in focus from revenue growth alone to the significant financial commitments and spending required to sustain it,” Ozkardeskaya said.

Investors are also closely watching Anthropic’s IPO for clues about rival OpenAI, which is seeking to raise $30 billion in what is expected to be its final private funding round before a potential IPO early next year. OpenAI recently secured $11 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation, below the $1.5 trillion it had initially sought.

The second half of the year has brought a reckoning for the AI boom, as investors question whether returns will justify the massive spending and mounting debt costs in an elevated ​interest-rate environment.

Concerns are also rising over the sustainability of the investment cycle, with questions around circular financing arrangements, the risk of infrastructure overcapacity and how quickly companies can turn their AI investments into revenue.

The Nasdaq notched its Deepest one-day drop in 19 months on Thursday, wiping out trillions in market value on ​fears of more AI scrutiny, particularly on data centre construction, after Democrats’ massive gains in the US midterm elections.

‘Harmful actions’

Despite the midterms being widely viewed as a rebuff to a White House which has aggressively supported the AI build-out and opposed regulations, Anthropic adopted President Donald Trump’s preferred name for the new technology, “Super Intelligence”, ‌at several points in ⁠its IPO filing.

Its filing spoke of a vision to “bring forth an age of miracles,” even as it warned of existential risks to humanity, laying bare the extraordinary promise and profound uncertainties at the heart of the AI boom.

The prospectus outlined a range of risks facing both the company and the technology, warning that competitors could gain an edge by developing models faster and that advances in AI could outpace Anthropic’s ability to put adequate safety and security measures in place.

“Our models have in the past behaved, and may in the future behave, in unintended, misaligned, or autonomous ways, including by taking harmful actions that no user or third party directed, which could adversely affect our reputation and brand, business, financial condition, and results of operations,” Anthropic warned in its latest prospectus.

The warnings come amid a growing number of incidents involving “rogue” AI agents that have escaped sandboxed environments and breached private company systems, alongside concerns that ​increasingly capable AI tools could be used by hackers to penetrate protected ​networks.

Growth comes with risks

Greater oversight and potential regulatory hurdles could complicate ⁠the infrastructure buildout underpinning the AI boom.

But Anthropic’s growth has so far defied those concerns, propelled by surging demand for its products, particularly its viral Claude models.

Anthropic’s run-rate revenue was roughly $81 billion as of October 31, up $10 billion from September 30, according to the IPO filing.

Anthropic’s net loss narrowed in the third quarter as revenue jumped 47% from a quarter earlier to $16.96 billion, though the pace of growth slowed. It had surged 144% in the prior ​quarter.

The company attributed the breakneck growth to the rapid adoption of Claude, including specialised products targeting industries such as healthcare, financial services and legal services.

Anthropic’s ambitions also come with enormous infrastructure costs. The company has ​nearly $900 billion in computing commitments with partners including ⁠Amazon and Alphabet’s Google, highlighting how its rapid growth depends on securing vast amounts of future computing capacity, some of which relies on financing beyond the company’s control.

The listing move follows Elon Musk’s SpaceX raising $75 billion in the world’s largest IPO in June, at a valuation of nearly $1.75 trillion, excluding additional shares purchased by underwriters through the greenshoe option.

Together with investments from cornerstones, which include Broadcom, Micron Technology, Microsoft and TSMC, the Anthropic share offering will raise a total of up to $90.4 billion.

Certain Anthropic board members and entities affiliated or associated with them have indicated interest in buying up to $303 million of shares from the offering.

Anthropic, locked in ⁠a fierce battle ​for market share with rival OpenAI, was last valued at $965 billion in a private funding round. The company’s prominent investors include Altimeter Capital, Dragoneer, Greenoaks and Sequoia Capital.

Anthropic, led by CEO ​Dario Amodei, was founded in 2021 by a group of researchers who left OpenAI following disagreements over governance and AI safety.

The shares are expected to trade on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol “ANT” after the IPO closes, which would make Anthropic one of the few major companies to go public this fall as higher borrowing costs, geopolitical turmoil and rising bond ​yields weigh on the IPO market.

Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are leading the syndicate of investment banks underwriting the offering.

headline: Blasts heard in Riyadh as Houthis claim strikes
description: Saudi-led coalition says it shot down a ballistic missile, two days after the Aramco Tower in the capital was hit
author: AFP
article_text:
Yemen’s rebel group Houthis on Tuesday claimed attacks targeting Saudi Arabia, including Riyadh’s airport and financial hub, further disrupting life in the region’s economic powerhouse.

In the early hours of the morning, AFP journalists heard blasts, while residents received a mobile-phone alert urging them to shelter from an “aerial threat”.

The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said it shot down a ballistic missile launched at the city by the group.

The incident came two days after the Houthis struck a psychological blow by hitting a skyscraper belonging to oil giant Aramco in Riyadh’s gleaming financial district.

Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree said the attacks had also targeted pumping stations along the East-West pipeline in Riyadh, an Aramco facility in the eastern Abqaiq region, as well as troops in Yemen.

Saudi Arabia, the world’s biggest oil exporter, has faced near-daily Houthi strikes since early October, including deadly attacks that closed Riyadh airport for two weeks.

A truce in Yemen’s long-running war between the Houthis and the Saudi-backed government unravelled in July.

Riyadh’s schoolchildren, after two days back in the classroom, returned to online learning on Tuesday “as part of the ongoing precautionary measures”, according to a message to parents on Monday evening.

On Monday, Saudi authorities said the East-West oil pipeline to the Red Sea was attacked in the Madinah region.

Saree labelled the Saudi claims “a blatant lie”, insisting the attack “targeted the East-West pipeline in the Saudi capital, Riyadh, not in Madinah”.

The export route has become vital for Saudi oil exports since Iran began hampering transit in the Strait of Hormuz, gateway to the energy-rich Gulf, in response to US-Israeli strikes.

Visible damage

The Houthi attacks have cast a shadow over attempts to overhaul the oil-reliant Saudi economy by attracting foreign investment and encouraging tourism and leisure spending.

Riyadh’s King Abdullah Financial District (KAFD) is one of the most visible manifestations of the drive, with towering glass skyscrapers, high-end retail outlets and green spaces dotting the area.

Images released by Saudi Arabia’s official press agency on Tuesday showed Riyadh officials inspecting the distinctively designed Aramco Tower, with visible damage to several of its floors.

Saudi authorities had earlier said the building was hit by falling shrapnel after an “attempted attack”.

The Houthis have repeatedly targeted Aramco tankers, refineries, storage areas and the company’s headquarters in Dhahran, on eastern Saudi Arabia’s Gulf coast.

In response, the coalition has been launching airstrikes against Houthi positions inside Yemen, with some attacks leaving dozens dead, according to the group.

On Tuesday, the Houthis’ news agency said Saudi warplanes carried out a series of strikes on the capital Sanaa and its outskirts, targeting a gas facility and a building belonging to the Yemeni state oil company.

One person was killed and three wounded in the attack on the gas facility, the Houthi health ministry said in a statement.

The coalition initially began fighting the Houthis in March 2015, months after the group seized Sanaa and forced out the government.

headline: US calls for new Europe security at Russia-Ukraine talks
description: Kushner says Washington has ‘narrowed the gaps’ as talks in Abu Dhabi continue on Wednesday, while Europe fears a deal over its head
author: AFP
article_text:
A first day of US-led talks between Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi ended on Tuesday, with Washington calling for a “new” security framework, as Europe fears US President Donald Trump plans a deal with Moscow on the continent’s future.

Trump’s envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff brought together the warring sides for several hours of negotiations — the first since February — that are set to continue on Wednesday.

Kushner told delegates the United States had “narrowed the gaps” between the sides — without providing details — and hoped to move towards a “solution” to Europe’s worst conflict since World War II.

In Paris, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio hailed the talks as “very productive” and called for Europeans to be eventually included at the negotiating table “because they are part of solving this problem”.

Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelensky later said the talks were “constructive and quite substantive”, saying his team reported to him that humanitarian issues and security guarantees were among what was discussed.

Speaking in Copenhagen, the Ukrainian president also said it was “time” for Europe to choose a representative for the talks.

Europe has been rattled as Trump has floated a deal with Russia on rewriting Europe’s post-war security, also worrying that Washington will force Kyiv to accept a de facto defeat.

At the Abu Dhabi talks, Trump’s son-in-law Kushner said the United States hoped to “create a new framework” of security between Ukraine, Russia and Europe that will secure “decades, if not centuries, of peace”.

Moscow, which several weeks before invading Ukraine issued an ultimatum to Western countries to roll back troops from eastern Europe, had also said this was a priority.

Ukraine has warned against a “Yalta 2.0”, referring to Western leaders dividing Europe with the Soviet Union after World War II, and the EU has said security arrangements can only be discussed after a ceasefire.

“Putin wants the USSR back,” Zelensky told Danish media.

Russia, which occupies swathes of its smaller neighbour, pummelled Ukraine with more attacks overnight, cutting power to thousands as temperatures plummet.

Putin has repeatedly turned down broader ceasefire offers and vowed his troops will press on in Ukraine.

Moscow pushes security review

In a sign it is serious about reviving its demand to review Europe’s decades-old security arrangement, Russia included a diplomat — Sergei Ryabkov — who logged Moscow’s pre-invasion demand for NATO to pull back from eastern Europe.

A Russian delegation source had said that settling the war was “merely one item on the agenda” and that Moscow’s main objective was reviewing security “for the entire continent”.

Kyiv’s chief negotiator Rustem Umerov met the US envoys and European, EU and NATO officials before the negotiations.

NATO’s general in Europe, Alexus Grynkewich, is also taking part.

In a joint statement, the Europeans, Ukraine, the United States and NATO reaffirmed their “shared commitment to a strong post-war European security architecture”.

Ukraine pushes for truces

Umerov said Kyiv’s priorities remained securing a ceasefire and security guarantees. “Our people are waiting to end this war,” he said.

As talks continued, Ukrainian and French foreign ministers in Paris commended US efforts to push for “partial truces”, which could serve as a “first step toward a complete and unconditional ceasefire”.

Last month, a local truce in Ukraine’s Kherson region brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump became the longest pause in fighting during the war.

Kyiv is also pushing post-war support for its army.

A senior Ukrainian source told AFP Ukraine wanted at least 10 years of financial support to sustain an 800,000-strong army able to defend any future Russian attack.

Land issue

There is huge distrust in Ukraine towards Trump’s aims.

The US leader hinted before the talks that Kyiv might have to give up land, saying: “They’re going to end up with a little bit different shape.”

Russia’s troops have advanced westward but have not been able to seize the whole of the coveted Donetsk region, and Moscow demands Kyiv surrender the parts of the embattled area it controls.

“Allowing Russia to decide the borders of Europe will be a huge mistake,” Denmark’s Mette Frederiksen said, as she hosted Zelensky on Tuesday.

The Ukrainian leader is due to meet other Nordic leaders in Denmark and earlier spoke to Finland’s Alexander Stubb, telling him Kyiv’s negotiators are doing their “best” to ensure talks “deliver results”.

Stubb is rumoured to be one of the contenders who could represent Europe at negotiations to end the war.

The Finnish leader and Norway’s Jonas Gahr Store held a rare phone call with Putin last month, which they called “frank and substantive”.

In a sign it is serious about reviving its demand to review Europe’s decades-old security arrangement, Russia included a diplomat — Sergei Ryabkov — who logged Moscow’s pre-invasion demand for NATO to pull back from eastern Europe.
A Russian delegation source had said that settling the war was “merely one item on the agenda” and that Moscow’s main objective was reviewing security “for the entire continent”.
Kyiv’s chief negotiator Rustem Umerov met the US envoys and European, EU and NATO officials before the negotiations.
NATO’s general in Europe, Alexus Grynkewich, is also taking part.
In a joint statement, the Europeans, Ukraine, the United States and NATO reaffirmed their “shared commitment to a strong post-war European security architecture”.
Ukraine pushes for truces
Umerov said Kyiv’s priorities remained securing a ceasefire and security guarantees. “Our people are waiting to end this war,” he said.

As talks continued, Ukrainian and French foreign ministers in Paris commended US efforts to push for “partial truces”, which could serve as a “first step toward a complete and unconditional ceasefire”.
Last month, a local truce in Ukraine’s Kherson region brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump became the longest pause in fighting during the war.
Kyiv is also pushing post-war support for its army.
A senior Ukrainian source told AFP Ukraine wanted at least 10 years of financial support to sustain an 800,000-strong army able to defend any future Russian attack.
Land issue
There is huge distrust in Ukraine towards Trump’s aims.
The US leader hinted before the talks that Kyiv might have to give up land, saying: “They’re going to end up with a little bit different shape.”
Russia’s troops have advanced westward but have not been able to seize the whole of the coveted Donetsk region, and Moscow demands Kyiv surrender the parts of the embattled area it controls.
“Allowing Russia to decide the borders of Europe will be a huge mistake,” Denmark’s Mette Frederiksen said, as she hosted Zelensky on Tuesday.

The Ukrainian leader is due to meet other Nordic leaders in Denmark and earlier spoke to Finland’s Alexander Stubb, telling him Kyiv’s negotiators are doing their “best” to ensure talks “deliver results”.
Stubb is rumoured to be one of the contenders who could represent Europe at negotiations to end the war.
The Finnish leader and Norway’s Jonas Gahr Store held a rare phone call with Putin last month, which they called “frank and substantive”.

headline: NAB issues second notice to Asad Mahmood over alleged illegal appointments
description: Former communications minister directed to appear on November 13 after anti-graft watchdog rejects his written response as unsatisfactory
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The National Accountability Bureau (NAB) has issued a second call-up notice to former federal minister for communications and postal services Asad Mahmood over alleged illegal appointments in the Pakistan Post Office Department, directing him to appear in person on November 13.

Asad Mahmood, the son of Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman, is being questioned in connection with alleged irregularities during his tenure as minister from 2022 to 2023.

NAB Rawalpindi is conducting an inquiry into alleged illegal appointments involving officers, officials and other individuals in the Pakistan Post Office Department.

The former minister had been directed to appear before NAB on November 10. However, he did not appear and instead submitted a written response through his lawyer.

NAB officials declared the response unsatisfactory and decided to summon him again.

According to the second call-up notice, Asad Mahmood has been directed to appear in person before NAB on Friday, November 13, 2026, at 11am.

The notice warned that failure to appear on the scheduled date could result in legal proceedings under Section 31 of the National Accountability Ordinance, 1999.

headline: PM vows energy independence as Chashma-5 nuclear plant hits milestone
description: Prime minister says nuclear power will cut reliance on imported fuels; 1,200MW plant expected to begin generation in September 2030
author: APP
article_text:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday called for building an economically strong, energy-independent and environmentally resilient Pakistan, saying the country would harness its resources, technology and human capital to secure a prosperous future.

Addressing the dome placement ceremony of the Chashma-5 Nuclear Power Plant (C-5) in Mianwali, the prime minister described the milestone as a testament to Pakistan’s determination to shape its future through hard work, technological advancement and strategic partnerships.

He said the project represented more than a construction milestone, describing it as a commitment to providing clean, reliable and affordable electricity to strengthen the economy and improve people’s lives.

PM Shehbaz said nuclear power would reduce Pakistan’s reliance on imported fuels and exposure to international price fluctuations while ensuring a stable electricity supply for industries, hospitals, educational institutions and households.

“Pakistan will not wait for anyone, but will build its own future through its hard work and untiring efforts,” he recalled saying at the project’s groundbreaking ceremony in July 2023.

The prime minister said the dome had been installed less than three and a half years after the groundbreaking, ahead of schedule. He expressed confidence that the plant would also be commissioned earlier than planned.

He stressed that Pakistan, as a climate-vulnerable country, had a responsibility to pursue energy solutions that supported economic development while protecting the environment.

Security, investment and economic revival

The prime minister said national security was essential for economic progress, adding that no country could build a prosperous future without safeguarding its present.

He acknowledged the role of the armed forces under the leadership of Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir in ensuring security and stability.

Referring to Pakistan’s experience during Marka-e-Haq, Shehbaz praised the professionalism, courage and resolve of the armed forces.

He said a secure environment was essential for attracting investment, reviving the economy and accelerating socioeconomic development.

The prime minister also appreciated Field Marshal Asim Munir’s support for the government’s economic revival and development initiatives.

Pakistan-China cooperation

PM Shehbaz described Chashma-5 as another enduring symbol of the strategic partnership between Pakistan and China, saying the project reflected the two countries’ shared commitment to economic progress.

He said it marked the seventh nuclear power unit China had helped Pakistan construct, highlighting the consistency of bilateral cooperation through challenging times.

The prime minister thanked Chinese President Xi Jinping, the Chinese government and the China National Nuclear Corporation for their continued support.

He also acknowledged the contributions of Chinese and Pakistani engineers involved in the project.

PM Shehbaz said the second phase of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) would create new economic opportunities, strengthen strategic ties and contribute to a brighter future for both countries.

He congratulated the Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission (PAEC), China Atomic Energy Authority, China National Nuclear Corporation, contractors, engineers, financial institutions and other stakeholders on the milestone.

The prime minister also thanked the people of Mianwali for hosting the project.

Nuclear power contributes 16.6% of electricity generation

Earlier, PAEC Chairman highlighted nuclear energy’s growing contribution to Pakistan’s electricity mix and energy security.

He said the country’s nuclear power plants were generating 3,530 megawatts of electricity safely and efficiently, helping avoid approximately 15 million tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions annually.

Nuclear energy accounts for around 16.6% of Pakistan’s electricity generation despite representing only 8.6% of its installed power capacity. Its share rises to approximately 26% during winter.

The Chashma-5 project will have a generation capacity of 1,200 megawatts and is expected to begin producing electricity in September 2030.

The ceremony was attended by Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, senior Pakistani officials, Chinese representatives and officials from relevant organisations.

PM Shehbaz concluded by reaffirming his government’s commitment to building an economically stronger, energy-secure and environmentally responsible Pakistan, expressing hope that Chashma-5 would remain a lasting symbol of Pakistan-China friendship and their shared aspirations for peace, stability and prosperity.

headline: Iran rejects France's 'baseless accusations' on cyberattack
description: Paris summons Iran’s ambassador, seeks EU sanctions and says it will ‘rule nothing out’ after attacks on supermarket fridges
author: AFP
article_text:
Iran on Tuesday said French accusations that it was responsible for cyberattacks on supermarket fridges last month were “baseless”.

“Iran’s foreign ministry categorically rejects the French government’s baseless and one-sided accusations against Iran regarding alleged cyber activities in France,” the ministry said in a statement.

It added that it “strongly condemns this hackneyed policy of levelling accusations against the Islamic Republic”.

Hundreds of French supermarkets were hit in the October 11 and 12 cyberattacks, which raised the temperatures in their refrigerators and freezers, forcing many to throw away entire inventories of perishable food.

Similar incidents were then reported in at least 11 other European countries in early November.

Along with summoning Iran’s ambassador and seeking European-level sanctions, French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said Tuesday that Paris would “rule nothing out and will take all measures – including those we may not disclose publicly – that we deem proportionate and necessary to deter any further attacks”.

Tehran meanwhile said it would “not hesitate to take necessary and appropriate measures to safeguard its national interests and security in the face of unlawful foreign activities”.

It added that France “is merely projecting its own governance failures” with these accusations.

Later in the day, Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi blamed the French government for the incident.

“Unable to manage fridges, let alone addressing grievances of its people, the French government is shifting blame for its failures onto others,” the top diplomat said on X.

Also on Tuesday, the European Union said it would look to provide a “swift and united response” pending discussion with member states after France’s announcement.

headline: Govt slashes petrol, diesel prices for sixth straight time
description: Petrol drops to Rs338 per litre and diesel to Rs371 as global oil prices hit two-month lows
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The federal government has reduced the price of petrol by Rs8 per litre to Rs338 and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs7 to Rs371, according to a notification.

Following the latest revision, petrol will cost Rs338 per litre, down from Rs346, while the price of HSD has fallen to Rs371 from Rs378.

The latest reduction follows a series of successive cuts announced by the government since November 2, as it continues to pass on relief amid changing international oil market conditions.

The Petroleum Division revises petroleum prices under the mechanism approved by the federal government, taking into account international oil prices, Platts rates, premiums and other associated costs.

Successive reductions in fuel prices

The latest cuts follow a series of reductions in petrol and diesel prices.

On November 7, the government reduced petrol prices by Rs6.59 per litre to Rs346 and HSD by Rs4.25 to Rs378.

On November 6, petrol became cheaper by Rs9.41 per litre to Rs352.59, while diesel prices fell by Rs5.56 to Rs382.25.

On November 4, the government cut petrol prices by Rs7.06 to Rs362 per litre and HSD by Rs3.71 to Rs387.81.

On November 3, petrol was reduced by Rs5.45 to Rs369.06 per litre, while diesel fell by Rs3.68 to Rs391.52.

The government had also reduced petrol prices by Rs3.40 per litre to Rs374.51 and HSD by Rs7.76 to Rs395.20 on November 2.

International oil prices

International oil prices fell about 2% on Tuesday, hitting fresh two-month lows after US officials played down the need for further military action against Iran, easing concerns over potential supply disruptions in the Middle East.

Brent crude futures fell $1.93, or 2.1%, to $90.64 a barrel at 10:28am ET (1528 GMT), while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude declined $1.44, or 1.7%, to $85.41.

Both benchmarks were on track for their lowest closes since August 28. On Monday, they had settled at their lowest levels since August 31.

headline: Republicans block bid to impeach Defence Secretary Hegseth
description: Democrats signal the fight could resume when they take control of Congress in January
author: Reuters
article_text:
Republicans in the US House of Representatives blocked an effort on Tuesday to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, winning a reprieve for the polarising Pentagon chief ​before Democrats take control of Congress next year and possibly try again.

The vote on a procedural motion came just hours after Hegseth blasted efforts to impeach him as ‌a farce and delivered a defiant defence of his record at the helm of the US military, winning praise from President Donald Trump.

The chamber voted 211 to 204 in favour of a motion to refer eight articles of impeachment to the Republican-led House Judiciary Committee, a move that the sponsor of the impeachment push, US Representative Thomas Massie, warned would kill it.

Massie, an outgoing Kentucky Republican, had hoped to draw votes from Republicans upset with Hegseth’s policies and wary of the unpopularity ​of the eight-month-old Iran war, but no other Republicans joined him.

The US-Israeli-led conflict has never been approved by Congress, which is the only branch of government constitutionally permitted to ​declare war.

Democrats had voiced strong support for the impeachment articles, which accuse Hegseth of the “high crimes and misdemeanours” of illegally ordering the military to wage war ⁠in Iran and Yemen, attack boats in the Caribbean Sea and abduct Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro in January.

But 11 Democrats, including former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi of California, did not vote.

If eight of ​them had, the procedural measure would have been defeated, paving the way for a full House impeachment vote.

Ian Krager, a spokesperson for Pelosi, said she had missed the vote because she had returned to San Francisco ​for an annual event to honour veterans, but would have voted against the procedural measure.

Trump cheered the results in a social media post, saying the effort to impeach Hegseth “has miserably FAILED!”

He wrote that Hegseth’s performance on Iran, Venezuela and other issues “led to the EXONERATION of a Great American Patriot.”

Hegseth would have been the first US defence secretary to be impeached. The last time any civilian leader of the US military was impeached was in 1876, when William Belknap held the ​title “secretary of war.”

Hegseth calls himself secretary of war, part of his effort to rebrand a military he said was too weak and “woke” when he took office last year.

Trump cannot change the name of the ​Defence Department without approval from Congress.

Iran war anger

Voter anger over the Iran war, which has settled into an effective stalemate focused on securing the Strait of Hormuz, helped Democrats win control of Congress in last week’s midterm elections.

A Reuters/Ipsos ‌poll published ⁠on Tuesday found a majority of Americans want the newly elected Democratic-majority US Congress, which takes office in January, to act to end the war with Iran once and for all.

Although Vice President JD Vance has publicly questioned the war and blamed it for the Republicans’ midterm rout, he voiced support for Hegseth on Tuesday.

“This isn’t about Iran, this is about the fact that Pete took on the bureaucracy at the Pentagon,” Vance wrote on social media.

Before the vote, House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries said on Monday: “Pete Hegseth has abused his power, undermined America’s national security, and he’s the architect of the reckless and costly failed war ​of choice in Iran.”

Hegseth has repeatedly defended the ​conflict, calling Trump courageous and saying Iran’s military ⁠has been left in ruins.

He also said his orders to US forces were lawful, despite Massie’s accusations of “high crimes and misdemeanours”.

“History will judge the Iran war quite differently than the conventional wisdom right now,” Hegseth said on Tuesday at his first Pentagon briefing in six months.

Jeffries said he would talk to ​members about whether to mount a new impeachment effort in the next Congress. “We’ll have that conversation at the appropriate time,” he said.

A Democratic-led push to ​impeach Hegseth could be far ⁠more intense, with lawmakers calling in top brass to testify, including generals and admirals fired by Hegseth who have remained silent so far.

Hegseth, who has railed against diversity efforts at the Pentagon, fired the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, who is Black, and the Navy’s top admiral, a woman, among others.

In such an effort, Democrats could also raise other issues of concern to voters, including Pentagon policy toward Ukraine and the US ⁠military’s strikes on ​suspected drug trafficking boats in Caribbean and Pacific waters.

Some Republicans say Hegseth’s strained relations with Congress are becoming a political liability ​as the Trump administration seeks a huge increase in the military’s budget to $1.5 trillion from $950 billion.

Massie said he was disappointed by the vote, comparing Republicans to passengers content to go down with the Titanic.

“They know it’s a sinking ship but committed to stay ​on board,” he said.
